report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Low-level filesystem removal primitives and the reparse-point-safe recursive tree walker.

symbols.name: _clear_readonly
symbols.note: Best-effort chmod to clear read-only bit; swallows OSError.

symbols.name: _unlink_reparse_point
symbols.note: Removes a reparse point link itself, trying rmdir then unlink (with chmod retry).

symbols.name: _force_unlink
symbols.note: Unlink with a chmod retry on PermissionError.

symbols.name: _force_rmdir
symbols.note: Rmdir with a chmod retry on PermissionError.

symbols.name: _chain_between
symbols.note: Builds the path chain from root to target by key comparison; raises ValueError if root is not an ancestor.

symbols.name: _remove_tree_no_follow
symbols.note: Recursively deletes root without traversing reparse points, with fresh verification before each syscall.

symbols.name: _verify_reachable
symbols.note: Nested closure inside _remove_tree_no_follow; re-checks all components above target for reparse points.

claims.text: Drop the read-only bit git sets on loose objects, best effort.
claims.why: The function chmods with S_IWRITE|S_IREAD and catches OSError without re-raising, matching 'best effort'.

claims.text: Remove the LINK itself. Never touches what it points at.
claims.why: Uses os.rmdir and os.unlink, which operate on the link itself, not the target; no follow is performed.

claims.text: A directory symlink / junction is removed with ``rmdir``, a file symlink with ``unlink``; which one applies differs by platform and link kind, so both are tried.
claims.why: The code tries os.rmdir first, then os.unlink, covering both cases; the chmod retry on unlink is a best-effort retry.

claims.text: ``[root, ..., target]``: every component ``target`` is reached THROUGH.
claims.why: The loop walks parent pointers from target up to root, collecting each component, then reverses, producing the full chain inclusive of both ends.

claims.text: Walked upward by comparison KEY rather than with ``relative_to``, which is case-sensitive and would raise on Windows for a differently-cased spelling.
claims.why: The loop compares _key(current) != _key(root) instead of using relative_to, so the claim about the method used is accurate.

claims.text: An uncaught ``ValueError`` is not a refusal, so the callers translate this one deliberately.
claims.why: The function raises ValueError when root is not on target's path; the caller (_verify_reachable) catches it and translates to WorktreeRemovalRace.

claims.text: Raises ``ValueError`` if ``root`` is not on ``target``'s path.
claims.why: The loop raises ValueError when parent == current before reaching root, which is exactly the condition where root is not an ancestor.

claims.text: Recursively delete ``root`` without ever traversing a reparse point.
claims.why: Every path is verified with _verify_reachable before use, and if a reparse point is found it is unlinked directly rather than descended into.

claims.text: THE INVARIANT ... EVERY path handed to a syscall that RESOLVES it -- ``os.scandir``, ``os.rmdir``, ``os.unlink``, ``os.chmod`` -- is re-classified with a FRESH ``lstat`` IMMEDIATELY beforehand, together with every component above it, up to and including ``guarded_ancestors``. There are exactly three such sites (the scan, the per-child unlink, the rmdir drain) and all three verify.
claims.why: The code shows only two verification sites: the pop-time check in the while loop (_verify_reachable(current)) and the per-child check (_verify_reachable(child)). The rmdir drain is not present in this chunk -- the drain loop is not shown, and the docstring itself later says 'the drain had no verification' until 2026-07-28, but in this chunk the drain code is not visible, so the claim that all three sites verify cannot be confirmed. Also, the chmod calls inside _force_unlink/_force_rmdir/_unlink_reparse_point are not preceded by a fresh verification, contradicting the claim that chmod is among the verified sites.

claims.text: No path in this function is acted on twice on the strength of one check.
claims.why: The retry paths in _force_unlink, _force_rmdir, and _unlink_reparse_point perform multiple syscalls on a single verification. For example, _unlink_reparse_point can do rmdir -> unlink -> chmod -> unlink, and _force_unlink does unlink -> chmod -> unlink, all after one verification at the call site. The docstring itself acknowledges this exception, so the claim as stated is false.

claims.text: ``shutil.rmtree`` is safe against a junction that is already in place and unsafe against one that appears mid walk; this function is safe against both.
claims.why: The comparison to shutil.rmtree's behavior is not verifiable from this chunk alone; it depends on external knowledge of shutil and on measurements referenced but not shown here.

claims.text: WHAT IS STILL NOT CLOSED ... The few microseconds between each fresh ``lstat`` and the ONE syscall that follows it.
claims.why: The code performs a fresh _verify_reachable (which does lstats) immediately before each syscall, but there is still a small window between the lstat and the syscall, as acknowledged.

claims.text: THE EXCEPTIONS TO "ONE VERIFICATION, ONE SYSCALL", NAMED PRECISELY ... * :func:`_force_unlink` / :func:`_force_rmdir` on ``PermissionError``: ``unlink`` -> ``chmod`` -> ``UNLINK AGAIN`` (resp. ``rmdir``). ... * :func:`_unlink_reparse_point`: ``rmdir`` -> ``unlink`` -> ``chmod`` -> ``unlink``, up to four syscalls on one verification.
claims.why: The code for _force_unlink does unlink, then on PermissionError chmod and unlink again. _force_rmdir does rmdir, then chmod and rmdir. _unlink_reparse_point tries rmdir, then unlink, then on OSError calls _clear_readonly (chmod) and unlink again. These match the described sequences.

claims.text: Re-verifying inside the retry was CONSIDERED AND NOT DONE this round
claims.why: The retry helpers do not call _verify_reachable; the docstring states this decision, and the code confirms no re-verification in those helpers.

claims.text: THE COST SCALES WITH DEPTH ... At depth 2-3, verifying before every syscall roughly doubles the walk. ... Against DEPTH, 400 files at the leaf ... depth 2 103 ms -> 320 ms 3.1x ... depth 20 129 ms -> 1380 ms 10.7x
claims.why: The performance measurements are not reproducible from this chunk; they depend on external benchmarks and the specific environment.

claims.text: The cost is NOT dominated by the ``lstat`` calls ... but by rebuilding the lexical chain in Python for every child, which is O(depth) per child
claims.why: The per-child loop calls _verify_reachable(child), which invokes _chain_between and walks up the hierarchy, so the chain construction is per child and O(depth). The lstat calls are part of that, but the chain building is the main cost as claimed.

claims.text: Raises ``OSError`` on failure and :class:`WorktreeRemovalRace` if a reparse point appears above ANY step -- the scan, the unlinks, or the drain. A partial delete is reported, never swallowed.
claims.why: The drain is not present in this chunk, and the docstring itself notes that until 2026-07-28 the drain had no verification, meaning a partial delete through a swapped ancestor was not reported. The current chunk does not show the drain code, so the claim that it now raises on reparse points above the drain cannot be confirmed. Also, the scan (os.scandir) is not preceded by a verification of the directory itself beyond the pop-time check, but that is covered; however, the drain is missing.

claims.text: A reparse point strictly above ``target`` redirects it wholesale, and unlinking that ancestor would delete a link the manager does not own, so this refuses instead of repairing.
claims.why: _verify_reachable checks every component above target (from guarded and above) and raises WorktreeRemovalRace if any is a reparse point, refusing rather than repairing.

claims.text: Does it exist at all? That is the only question answered here. Whether a path is a reparse point, a file, or a directory is decided in exactly ONE place -- when it is POPPED, immediately before it is opened -- and the root is not special-cased.
claims.why: The comment says classification happens in exactly one place (when popped), but the per-child loop also classifies each child with a fresh lstat before acting, and the root is classified via os.lstat(root) before the loop. That is a second classification site for the root, contradicting 'exactly ONE place'. The comment claims the root is not special-cased, but os.lstat(root) is a separate classification before the pop-time check.

claims.text: RE-CHECK 1 OF 3 (the others are in the entry loop and the drain, and each one is separately load-bearing -- see the mutation notes).
claims.why: The comment says there are three re-checks: the pop-time, the entry loop, and the drain. In this chunk, only two are visible (pop-time and per-child in the entry loop). The drain is not shown, so the claim of three sites cannot be verified, and the docstring earlier admits the drain had no verification until recently.

claims.text: A FRESH lstat, deliberately not entry.stat(): on Windows the DirEntry's stat is served from this scandir's cache (measured), so asking the DirEntry would re-introduce the stale read.
claims.why: The code calls _verify_reachable(child) and then os.lstat(current) or _force_unlink, not entry.stat(), so the claim about avoiding the cache is consistent with the code.

claims.text: HONEST NOTE ON THIS BRANCH: mutation testing shows the suite does NOT go red if it is deleted, and that is not an oversight in the tests -- it is redundant on this platform, measured both ways. A junction is reported as a directory by is_dir(follow_symlinks=False), so it would be queued and then unlinked by the pop-time check; a directory symlink is NOT, so it would fall to _force_unlink, and os.unlink removes a Windows directory symlink without following it (measured: link gone, target intact).
claims.why: The mutation testing results and platform-specific behavior of os.unlink on directory symlinks are not verifiable from this chunk alone; they rely on external measurements and Windows-specific semantics not demonstrated here.

claims.text: There is no check that cannot fail in this chunk
claims.why: All checks in the visible code have reachable failure paths (e.g., _verify_reachable can raise ValueError, os.lstat can raise FileNotFoundError, os.scandir can raise OSError, etc.). No tautological assertions are present.

claims.text: There is no refusal with no reachable repair in this chunk
claims.why: The WorktreeRemovalRace refusals are deliberate and do not name a repair; they are terminal errors. No refusal names a fix that another rule forbids.

claims.text: There is no rule inverted with respect to its own stated goal in this chunk
claims.why: The verification logic blocks the narrow action of unlinking through a reparse point and permits the broad action of removing the link itself, which is consistent with the stated goal of not touching the target.

claims.text: There is no value parsed from output whose format is not pinned in this chunk
claims.why: No output parsing occurs in this chunk; all operations are filesystem syscalls.

observations.what: The docstring claims exactly three verification sites, but only two are visible in this chunk; the drain is not present, and the docstring itself acknowledges the drain was previously unverified.

The retry paths (_force_unlink, _force_rmdir, _unlink_reparse_point) perform multiple syscalls per verification, contradicting the 'one verification, one syscall' invariant as stated in the docstring, though the docstring later acknowledges this exception.
The comment claiming classification happens in exactly one place is contradicted by the explicit os.lstat(root) before the loop, which is a separate classification site.

risks: _remove_tree_no_follow | high | The invariant claim of three verification sites cannot be confirmed because the drain is not in this chunk; if the drain lacks verification, a partial delete through a swapped ancestor could go unreported, as the docstring admits was the case until recently. | Inspect the remainder of _remove_tree_no_follow to see whether the drain loop calls _verify_reachable before each rmdir.
